name: Asta

psychological_experiences.evidence: Born without magic in the Clover Kingdom, where magical power determines social rank. Mocked by nobles (e.g., Sekke) and dismissed at the Grimoire Acceptance Ceremony when no grimoire first appears. His response across the early arcs is never despair — it is training: thousands of push-ups, sword drills, body built to compensate for what magic would have given.

The five-leaf grimoire chooses him only when Yuno is attacked at the ceremony — power arrives through protective fury, not ambition. Against Vetto, beaten near death, he keeps standing until anti-magic awakens; against Dante and Lucifero, the smile cracks into devil-union rage. The optimism holds until it cannot, and what surfaces underneath is fury.
psychological_experiences.tag: optimism as armor over unprocessed rage

psychological_experiences.evidence: Licita, his mother, abandoned him at the Hage church as an infant because her body drained the life of anyone she touched — abandonment as protection. He never knew her. Liebe, the devil in his grimoire, is likewise magicless among devils and was saved by Licita: the story shows Asta who he is by showing him his mirror. The grief is unnamed because its object was never named to him.

Raised alongside Yuno at the church; their rivalry is mutual fuel spoken as affection ('he's my rival'). When Yuno receives the four-leaf grimoire, Asta celebrates without envy. The Black Bulls — the disgraced, rowdy squad no one wanted — become a found family that chooses him. Despite abandonment, he attaches securely and repeatedly.

His stated goal from childhood: become Wizard King. Every arc re-commits to it. The story has not yet tested the deeper question — who Asta is if the title never comes — which keeps the striving honest rather than resolved. The want is explicit; the need (worth apart from the crown) is the open question.
psychological_experiences.tag: identity fused with an unattained goal

representation_notes: Asta subverts the 'loud idiot protagonist' stigma: his emotional intelligence is high — he reads people accurately, defuses tension, and forges bonds across class lines. The class critique has teeth (peasant orphan vs. magic aristocracy), and the story mostly avoids the 'hard work beats talent' trap by giving Yuno equal genius and equal grind, keeping the rivalry honest. Shonen optimism is shown with its cost, not as a cure-all.
